title: Relative associated points under arbitrary base change
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a locally finite type morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and $g:S'\to S$ any morphism. Form $X'=X\times_SS'$ with projections $g':X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to S'$ [def-pc-base-change], and put $\mathcal F'=(g')^*\mathcal F$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. For a point $z\in X$ with $r=f(z)$, say $z\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X/S}(\mathcal F)$ if the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{X_r,z}$ is the annihilator of a nonzero element of $(\mathcal F_r)_z$ [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes; def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], where $\mathcal F_r$ is the pullback to the fibre $X_r$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Define $\operatorname{Ass}_{X'/S'}(\mathcal F')$ in the same way. If $z'\in X'$ maps to $z\in X$, $r'\in S'$ and $r\in S$, then $z'\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X'/S'}(\mathcal F')$ if and only if $z\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X/S}(\mathcal F)$ and $z'$ is a generic point [def-sc-generic-point] of an irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] of the fibre over $z$ of $X'_{r'}\to X_r$, identified with $\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(r')\otimes_{\kappa(r)}\kappa(z))$. Here residue fields are [def-weil-residue-field], $\operatorname{Spec}$ is [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and tensor products are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] (for algebras the multiplication is $(a\otimes b)(c\otimes d)=ac\otimes bd$).

proof.text: Put $k=\kappa(r)$, $k'=\kappa(r')$, $Y=X_r$, $Y'=X'_{r'}$ and $\mathcal G=\mathcal F_r$. Apply [lem-trf-base-change-fibre-flat-qcoherent]: the canonical $h:Y'\to Y$ is flat, $Y$ is locally Noetherian, $\mathcal G$ is quasi-coherent, and $\mathcal F'_{r'}\cong h^*\mathcal G$. These are exactly the hypotheses and coefficients needed for flat pullback.

By [lem-trf-flat-pullback-associated-points], $\operatorname{Ass}_{Y'}(\mathcal F'_{r'})=\bigcup_{y\in\operatorname{Ass}_Y(\mathcal G)}j_y(\operatorname{Ass}_{Y'_y}(\mathcal O_{Y'_y}))$. A point in the image of $j_y$ maps to $y$ under $h$. Thus the given point $z'\in Y'$ is associated if and only if the canonical point $\bar z\in Y$ over $z$ is associated to $\mathcal G$ and the corresponding point of $Y'_{\bar z}$ is associated to its structure sheaf.

Apply [lem-trf-base-change-residual-fibre-cm] to $f,g,r',z$. It identifies $Y'_{\bar z}$ and its point corresponding to $z'$ with $\operatorname{Spec}T$ and its distinguished point, where $T=k'\otimes_k\kappa(z)$. It also gives that $T$ is Noetherian and its prime localizations are Cohen–Macaulay; only $\kappa(z)/k$ needs to be finitely generated, and $k'/k$ remains arbitrary.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-cm-affine-associated-generic] to $T$ from step 3. Association of its distinguished point is equivalent to that point being generic in an irreducible component of $\operatorname{Spec}T$. Substitute in step 2. By the fibrewise definition [def-trf-relative-assassin], association of $\bar z$ to $\mathcal F_r$ and association of $z'$ to $\mathcal F'_{r'}$ are precisely membership in the two relative assassins. This gives both directions of the stated equivalence.

lean.statement: theorem relativeAssassin_baseChange_iff {X S S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (g : S' ⟶ S) (z' : ↑(Limits.pullback f g)) : z' ∈ relativeAssassin (Limits.pullback.snd f g) ((tensorPullback (Limits.pullback.fst f g)).obj F) ↔ Limits.pullback.fst f g z' ∈ relativeAssassin f F ∧ ∃ Z ∈ irreducibleComponents (Spec (Scheme.Pullback.Triplet.ofPoint ((pullbackSymmetry f g).hom z')).tensor), IsGenericPoint (Scheme.Pullback.SpecOfPoint ((pullbackSymmetry f g).hom z')) Z
